Welcome rob - I have to say that trying to explain a strange sighting to anyone who has
never seen anything strange or doesn't have an open mind can be a daunting experience
even for someone not in the limelight.

People just assume you're a bit crackers if you speak about something that isn't mundane
or is out of the ordinary.

I never really took much notice about what the papers said, until I saw them taking the
mickey out of your desire to explore some of the stranger things that happen - but then I
was disgusted with them.

Back to the topic, I live in the far south west of the UK and have seen a couple of things
that just defy explanation - cornwall has a bit of a rep for strange occurrences, like UFO's
and paranormal experiences link to the cornwall UFO triangle

I've tried to rationalize what I've seen, and have only spoken about one experience, even
here on ATS, although I also posted some photo's my borther took.

The thing is, people are always quick to mock what they don't understand, and for that
reason, I've kept my gob shut with all but the most open minded of my friends.

I respect your coming here and sharing your experiences, and I hope you have a great
time here.

hunter...always looking out for them) I had a Land Rover which I had painted part
completely black apart from the front and back ends which I painted with black and yellow
chevron stripes.

You seeing a craft with that is a bit of a surprise to be honest. That's the first I've ever
heard of a design like that. What makes it more interesting is that black and yellow is
natures way of saying "DON"T TOUCH"...

Everywhere I whent I could leave the landie unlocked and nothing ever whent missing..
kinda funny.

Secondly, the ball of light that shot straight up.. I've experienced very similar whilst living
in France.

It was 4am when I suddenly woke from sleep and sat bolt upright in bed. I looked out the
Velux (roof) window and saw a large ball of white light. It shrank down to about the size
of pea/grape then moved to the left for a short distance and then shot straight up out
into space.

A few weeks later, I was in the back yard at about 11pm when I saw a ball of white light
come over a hill, fly down into the valley. It carried on over the valley and then it just
suddenly disappeared.

Took me a while to work out exactly how the first object shrank in size... it was moving
directly away from my line of site. It had to have been hovering and somehow realised I
was looking. This is the only way I can explain how it backed away from me. It knew I was
awake and looking.
All my pictures of my landie are in the UK at the moment including all my paperwork from
when I was involved with the UFO group. But, if you are in anyway in need of me
providing something to back this up, I do have a couple of links I can provide for
reference.

Hi - well seems to have been quite an eventful day...

I am curious though - have you (Robbie) seen any video clips or photographs that are in
anyway similar to what you saw that day - as your description sounds fairly specific and
unique to any that I have come across so far?

The recent trend as far as I see it has been a spate of pretty professional cgi clips to
horribly amateur cgi clips to the more compelling images of lights in the sky (that can't be
readily cast aside as lanterns)

These video clips in Saltcoats (Scotland) and of course Phoenix seem to be of a particular
(popular model) type of craft- a 21st century design perhaps? Perhaps what you saw was
the test model...

I find it fascinating how a lot of images of ufos tend to reflect the graphical and aesthetic
design culture of the decade that they were taken in with the odd exception of course -
which is where your description comes in, I think it'd be really interesting to get your
friends who witnessed this to recall their descriptions also - it may bring forward other
witnesses perhaps with photographic evidence who have keeping schtum till now..

Anyway - I applaud you for speaking out

ps I'm not a Rangers fan but sorry on behalf of Scotland for what they did to your home
town! Stay happy and keep writing - berth

reply to post by ufopunx

If you reported a sighting, I would accord you the same level of acceptability. I would not
discount it on what was NOT available, but looked at instead the information that was
brought to the table. Speculating on unavailable data reeks of a preconceived opinion.

This is not the only time on these forums where I have seen people have their stories
picked at like a bunch of hungry turkeys going after one oddball fowl in the group.

And you will note that I mentioned no names in my post. I wasn't aiming my post at you,
and if it seemed that way, you have my apology. This type of "investigative logic" feeds on
itself, with people resorting to all types of convoluted reasoning to discredit the report,
and like a snowball rolling down hill, it becomes a feeding frenzy contributed to by many.
and like a snowball rolling down hill, it becomes a feeding frenzy contributed to by many.

I agree, were this an unknown member, I doubt the page count would have been so high,
but about half of that is just the gushing of those dazzled by a bit of fame. The fact that
RW is a celebrety makes no real difference, as UFOs have been reported by people in all
walks of life.

However, you reveal something of a suspicious nature, if not a debunker clutching for a
straw, with your comment on drugs and drinking. To someone taking an unbiased
approach to this, your comment would sound like another sideways swipe at the integrity
of the witness. Were you at present? If not, then the "question" about the sobriety of RW
at the time comes off as another snide way of casting a pall on the report without actually
having anything of substance with which to properly discredit it.

If you lack suffecient insight into why I say this, then you haven't read enough government
documents relating to UFOs where the same baseless (meaning without any reasonable
evidence) accusations and implied accusations are used to discredit witnesses. It seems to
be a favorite tool in the war against serious UFO study.

As a long time UFO researcher, (amature variety), I am less than enthralled by those that
want to devour a witness before there is any evidence of foul play on their part. Even
vultures have the dencency to wait till life leaves the body to start in.

To me this is simply another eyewitness report of a possible UFO event. Nothing more and
nothing less. It also has no greater standing than any other report, and is discussion
worthy mainly for the "black light" portion of the report, IMO.

reply to post by David H N

I don't want to get off topic here but sacred geometry and harmonics seem to be involved
in pretty much everything else so I would like to explore what it could mean in regards to
UFO sightings and the likes.

I believe that physical reality is mathematical by definition. A geometric design based on
numbers that repeat in cycles in order to create the phenomenon of linear time. You see
geometry everywhere in nature. Many people, myself included, see the numbers 11:11
frequently and report synchronicities around it. The best way I can describe it is as if it
creates a tiny rift in the time fabric and opens a portal or connection to multiple
dimensions. When I see the numbers it's like time stops.

If UFOs are of a much higher frequency than humans then our physical senses cannot
detect them. But sometimes we obviously do. So what is it that happens at those
occasions that lowers their frequency (or raise ours?) so that we can detect them? Is it
that the time dimension is somehow transcended? Or is it that they don't really "get" our
time dimension, being something very particular for planet Earth, and just get it wrong
from time to time? We always seem to glorify ETs as being superior but is it possible that
they too can miscalculate for the simple reason that they are unfamiliar with linear time?

Regarding the 11:11 I'd love to discuss that in more detail. Maybe we can make a new
thread somewhere more appropriate?

This topic has been with me for many years and I have had the occasional "he's a nutter"
thrown my way.

But, I've had more people want to talk to me about my experiences or at least ask
questions to settle their own minds.

My old land rover had the name of the UFO group I was involved in painted in big yellow
letters all down the each side..you couldn't miss the three letters UFO.

I had loads of people wave at me with a genuine smile. I'd find people waiting in the car
parks next to the landie hoping I'll come back soon so they can have a chat.

My closest friends swear blind I'm from another planet....

Regardless of what the press says, good or bad, it is the experience that you have had and
shared with those around you that gives you all the knowledge that you are not crazy, off
the wall, lost, misguided, brainwashed or intoxicated in any other manner... What has
happened has happened and nothing will ever change that.

There are so many who want to believe and literally pray to be shown something, though
they may never get to experience anything. Which is a bit of a shame, but that's the way
it goes I guess.

No matter what's said, I, and a lot of others here on ATS are with you and will stand by
you in OUR search for the truth on the matter.

Publicly backing down and keeping quiet will only show that those who want to keep a lid
on things, have managed to do so yet again.

Did the 'passion of christ' stop Mel Gibson from making films? No..
Did the reports and criticism stop Charlie Sheene from expressing his views and supporting
others of the alternative events of 911? No...

Very glad to have you with us...

posted on May, 17 2008 @ 06:22 PM                                                       link

Hi Rob.

I have also witnessed some kind of weird spotlight-like UFO's. I have not written about it
until now.

Actually this was one of the reasons I joined ATS. I am normally a very sceptical person
and even though I (for logical reasons) believed in life somewhere else in the universe, I
was not really a believer in UFO's until I saw these strange lights a couple of years ago.

People might say, maybe they were spotlights in the sky, but the strange thing was that it
sort of followed me around. I first noticed it when I was taking a walk. I looked up and
saw these strange lights in the sky that sort of moved around. I assumed they were some
kind of spotlights but I could not see the actual beam. They were moving around in a
strange pattern. I shrugged it off however and went home to my apartment... However, I
was shocked to see the lights had (I guess) followed me, because when I looked out they
were outside my window !!! in the sky, moving around in a specific way.

This really freaked me out. I tried to find a logical explanation and I went outside again
and took a walk, sort of afraid to even look up at the sky.

After a few blocks I did however, and I saw them again, above me, moving in the same
way. I then went home and closed the curtains and I didn't look out.

People might say, why not even take a photo or something? The answer is I was kinda
shocked. I was not at the time a UFO believer. I just wanted to -not- see it and forget
it... and anyway, sadly it was not some spectacular UFO in different colours. They were
strange lights, grey-ish in colour (like spotlights but without the beam) but they apparently
followed me and moved in a specific pattern like way.

This was my only UFO sighting ever had and I have not witnessed any more since this
incident (a few years ago).


This happened in Stockholm Sweden by the way. Sorry about my crappy english, it's not my
first language...

Just a question for the crowd, and it'll probably get lost in the mass of replies, but I'm
curious what other experiences people have had in about the same time range (5 months
ago I think).
ago I think).

As for myself, the only "alien" experience I ever had was 6 summers ago. My family was
living in tents at the time as were beginning to build a house. This took place in Port
Angeles, WA (couple hours west of Seattle. I was just walking around our property that
night waiting for the Northern lights that were forecasted to show that week (which is
rare in Washington). While I was walking around I was thinking about the night sky,
singing my thoughts aloud, one of those rare moment when I simply felt in tune with the
universe.

The Aurora had been going on for awhile when suddenly like a switch it was "turned off"
and a bright light appeared in the sky, almost like a spotlight straight at me for an
instant. I could tell that whatever it was had just entered the atmosphere and it was
somewhat smaller than the moon.

Say this O is the moon, this o is the object I saw, and this . is a star.

I startled me and I stopped singing. Then the object sped off directly for Seattle. At first I
thought it must have been a meteorite, but the size of it frightened me so much I wasn't
sure what to think. I've seen plenty of meteors enter the atmosphere and just burn off,
but my instinct told me that this object had definitely entered without burning to dust.
Yet I heard nothing about it after that even though I made my way about the web asking
questions everywhere I could. That was before I came across ATS.

Anyhow, don't want to steal Robbie's thunder. I just thought I'd share because I've been
wondering about it ever since and the music part of both experiences had me thinking
about it again.

Hey folks,

I was also there on 'the night of the Black Light'
Rob's account of events is pretty much how I remember it too.
Nobody was drunk or high. There was a good vibe though.
I remember at one point, the lights in the sky were unusual in shape and moving at
seemingly impossible speeds. We were all a bit transfixed at the wonder of it all and how
strange it was that the song Arizona ( about abduction and lies in the desert) seemed to
encourage the sky to be more active. We were excited to say the least.
After the activity had died down we scoured the internet for any sightings but with no
joy.
The other thing we saw was beyond my imagination
The black light was like a dense thick flash of lightening in negative, about 20-25 feet in
length. It seemed to enter the room and leave in a nanosecond.
We all saw it and said ' What the **** was that?'
" Did everyone just see black lightening come into the room and then disappear?'
'Yes!' the response was unanimous.
Strange I know. I'm still astounded by it all. Thanks for reading.

    8 March 2008 News:

    www.robbiewilliams.pl...
    Robbie Williams has revealed he’s about to quit his pop career… to become a
    full-time UFO chaser! Williams, currently on strike from record label EMI, was
    being interviewed by singer Joss Stone when he made the weird confession,
    telling her he’d been visited by little green men three times.

    “Seriously, I want to go out and investigate these things. I’m stopping being a pop
    star and being a full-time ufologist. “We could be like Mulder and Scully in real
    life,” he told her. “You’re always mega-busy, but I’ve got nothing on at the
    minute.” ... added that the first time he’d seen a UFO was when he was a kid,
    but had had two other “close encounters” that were more recent. “I was at the
    Beverly Hills Hotel and I was lying on my sun lounger outside at night, looking
    up,” he said. “Then, about 300 foot above me, there was this square thing which
    just passed over my head silently and then shot off.” It gets better… “The next
    one was the weirdest one yet. I’d just written a song called Arizona, and it’s all
    about alien contact and I was playing that,” ... “I stood on the balcony and there
    was this big ball of gold light that turned up - we thought it was Venus or Mars or
    something. Then the song stops playing and it disappears. But then we put
    Arizona on again and the ball turned back up. It happened four times. “After that a
    massive electrical storm started and these two big massive balls of light started
    dancing in the sky. It was like a whole light show for about an hour.” Warming to
    his theme..... goes on to describe the time he was in a recording studio and saw
    a “big strip of black light” miraculously appear in the room. “It was three inches
    thick and it shot from one end of the room out of the window,” he claimed. “It’s
    absolutely bonkers. It’s something to do with LA.”

    Understandably, realises his comments are unlikely to be well received. “People
    will think, ‘This geezer’s been in rehab, he’s off his head’,” he predicted, before
    adding: “How mental are they going to make me out in the papers.” Erm, very? ...
    even reveals that he’s set up Google news alerts on UFOs so he can get his
    daily fix of all things extraterrestrial. “What I am excited about is there’s more and
    more every day and it’s gathering speed,” he says.

Take a mirage for example, people seeing things that just are'nt there, but are convinced
they are.

Could anything like that have happened to recreate the illusion of this dark light we are
discussing?

Whilst doing searches for "dark lightning", i found info on like a negative effect being
produced in photography called the "Clayden effect".

Heres an example....scroll down the page for the piccy i'm reffering to....

Clayden effect

     
     "Clayden effect....

     An old photography book I have mentions the Clayden effect as being still unexplained.
     Strong, quickly moving lights will sometimes reverse on the photo. The book showed
     photos of sparks flying. Most where white, but a few sparks were totally black. I suppose
     that what I got on this photo is the same effect! I was photographing insects dancing on
     the water, and only on one of the 10 photos I made I got these totally saturated, white
     lines with sharply defined edges. The strong light was provided by the sun reflecting on
     the water, and the motion by the water itself. It's pretty logical that on reversal film the
      Clayden reversion produces white instead of black streaks!

      This is a very rare happening. I have not been able to intentionally obtain the Clayden
      effect on any photo."


I'm sure the above effect has little if nothing to do with real life incidents, but if light can
effect the way we see things on film, could this not be possible in real too?

I have very little knowledge in both photography or environmental effects on the way we
see things, so excuse me if any of what i amsuggesting is not possible.

Could the dark light Rob saw, actualy have been normal bright colour, yet something that
night made it appear dark?

Ok it still leaves a lot unexplained, but i'm just clutching at straws.

CX.

Truth be told, we know very little about electromagnetism and even less about gravity.
Any engineer or scientist worth their salt will admit we do not know exactly what
electromotive force is, even though we use it on a consistent basis.

Furthermore, if you are a fan of Prof. Lisa Randall, you may be aware her theories depict
the universe (our universe) as a four dimensional construct or bubble trapped within a ten
dimensional superspace. I find this particulary fascinating, as a 4:6 split (a very popular
book on this subject was written some time ago called The Crack in the Cosmic Egg)
reduces to a 2:3 ratio, consistent with, of all sources, the Biblical creation story.

When we contemplate the multidimensional aspects of our reality, then we can see how
experiences like Robbie's can fit into the new worldview. In "olden" days these were signs
and portents, and based upon the newly revealed knowledge of the ancients, they appear
to be closer to the truth than we realize.

In my opinion, Robbie is telling the truth. As an analogy, he and his friends have seen the
curve of the Earth, and he wishes to share his experience with those of us who see it as
flat. It is up to us to exercise our gifts in order to understand.

One of the things that has so far not been considered in relation to the music is that the
effect was not on the "UFO" but on RW and his friends.

Considered in this light, UFOs could be buzzing about unseen, cloaked or whatever, and it
was the music, perhaps certain tones or frequencies, that opened the perception of them
to those emmersed in the music.

Such a thing would explain the reports of people seeing UFOs from their cars, yet other
people on the same road seem to show no reaction, as if they saw nothing. It could be
that there was a certain tone played in the vehicle that caused those who heard it to be
more perceptive, while other cars had different sounds that did not match the needed
pattern for recognition to take place.

Not saying that this is so, just passing along an idea that occurred to me. If this was true,
then such a song as "Arizona" might have a chord, or combination of chords, that
increased mental awareness in the listener/participant.

Maybe that song needs to be made after all.
